interface.name: alroot_gpu_buffer_v1
interface.description: A vendor-independent alternative to Linux DRM DMA-BUF for Android GPUs that can create AHardwareBuffers but cannot export them through GBM or linux-dmabuf. The producer transfers an existing, fully allocated AHardwareBuffer over an AF_UNIX socket using the public Android NDK AHardwareBuffer_sendHandleToUnixSocket method. The compositor obtains it using AHardwareBuffer_recvHandleFromUnixSocket, creates a wl_buffer, imports the buffer directly into Vulkan as a VkImage and GPU-composites the image into its Android swapchain. No direct scanout is implied. The producer retains and synchronizes its own reference. Once the compositor is done sampling, wl_buffer.release permits reuse. Unlike banner_ahb_v1 this path never requires a DRM buffer, DRM node, modifier, Qualcomm layout, or a private native_handle structure. Version 1 accepts only Android AHardwareBuffer RGBA8. Version 2 supports an optional BGRA8 allocation when the compositor has tested that its Android gralloc and Vulkan driver can import it. A version-2 global is never advertised without that runtime test. This does not change the legacy version-1 create_buffer contract. Version 3 adds per-commit producer readiness. It is advertised only when version-2 format support and Vulkan GPU sync_file import are both available. Storage with explicit readiness is externally owned in GENERAL layout; the compositor acquires it from FOREIGN, and returns it to FOREIGN/GENERAL before allowing reuse.

request.name: create_buffer

description.summary: transfer an AHB and create a usable wl_buffer

request.description: The socket is prefilled with the AHardwareBuffer handle. The passed width and height must match the actual AHardwareBuffer description. A successful creation generates a wl_buffer whose release events follow ordinary Wayland compositor lifetime rules.

request.name: create_buffer_with_format

description.summary: submit RGBA8 or optional BGRA8 AHardwareBuffer

request.description: The format is the Android AHardwareBuffer format from the advertised format enum. The compositor validates that it matches the imported buffer's real description, GPU-sampling usage and VkImage import capability. Version-1 clients must continue to use create_buffer, which accepts RGBA8 only.

request.name: set_acquire_fence

description.summary: set producer completion for the next surface commit

request.description: The fence applies only to the next wl_surface.commit, which must newly attach the specified native AHB wl_buffer. The producer must release its writes and storage to external GENERAL ownership before signalling this sync_file. The compositor waits on the GPU before accessing it. Replacing uncommitted readiness closes the prior FD. A commit without a new attachment keeps its existing dependency. wl_buffer.release is withheld until all committed producer work and all compositor reads have completed, including discarded commits. The server owns the received FD. Clients close their local FD after marshalling. A signalled-export value of -1 is not a Wayland FD; use set_acquire_ready instead. No readiness request retains the legacy producer-completed contract for a newly attached buffer.

request.name: set_acquire_ready

description.summary: set an already completed external producer use

request.description: Same next-commit and buffer-identity contract as set_acquire_fence, with producer completion already established. Storage still uses the external FOREIGN/GENERAL ownership contract. This also covers a successful Vulkan SYNC_FD export returning the signalled value -1.

entry.name: unsupported_format
entry.summary: AHB lacks GPU sampling or RGBA8

entry.name: invalid_sync
entry.summary: invalid acquire sync_file, surface, or commit state
